summary: Intermittent long-tail timeouts when output_as_json returns large arrays
summary_short: Timeouts on requests that emit large JSON arrays via output_as_json
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLedger reports ~2-5% of inference requests using output_as_json (array-heavy responses) end with 504/timeout or very long tail latencies (>10s). Impact: production traffic hitting enterprise plan, visible in us-east and occasionally in eu-west.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints see intermittent user-perceived timeouts.
- Elevated error rates correlate with requests that serialize arrays with >1000 elements.

Environment:
- prod - us-east primary; also reproducible in eu-west staging less frequently.
- Model in use: redwood-instruct-3b, token length ~150–900, streaming response enabled, output_as_json flag set to true.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a generation request to the /v1/generate endpoint with output_as_json:true and a prompt that instructs the model to enumerate ~1500 items (example prompt attached).
2) Enable streaming.
3) Observe client socket remains open while server completes generation; in some cases, finalization step stalls and client receives a 504.

Observed behavior:
- Long CPU spike (~70–90% on the postprocess thread) when serializer flattens and validates large arrays.
- Streaming chunk delivery continues, but finalization (closing JSON structure and validation) can take multiple seconds and sometimes exceeds gateway timeout, returning 504.
- SRE dashboard shows elevated GC events on the front-end proxy pod during these requests.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming responses with output_as_json should keep tail latency bounded and not timeout in normal load. Finalization should be O(n) without sudden CPU/GC spikes.

Logs / artifacts:
- Trace: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/72a1f4b3
- Kibana query: kbn://prod-logs/app/kibana#/discover?_g=()&query=service:%22json-postprocess%22%20AND%20http.status_code:504
- Attached sample request payload and client SDK log snippet (customer provided).
steps_to_reproduce: Use output_as_json:true and request generation of >1000 list elements
Observe request duration and gateway timeout
observed_behavior: Final JSON close/validation takes multiple seconds
Intermittent 504s at gateway despite tokens delivered over stream
Postprocess worker CPU spikes and GC activity
expected_behavior: Finalization completes quickly and keeps request under SLA
Streaming clients receive a clean JSON stream without server timeouts
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Jamie Ortega (Support): Customer BrightLedger opened ticket after 3 user complaints in last 24h. They see 2-5% of calls failing with 504 when generating large arrays.
2026-03-10 10:03 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Initial triage shows correlation between array size and error rate. We reproduced a 6s spike on json-postprocess in us-east when generating 1500-element array.
2026-03-11 14:20 - Customer (BrightLedger): Provided sample prompt and SDK logs. Note: this happens with both node and python SDKs, and disabling streaming reduces but does not eliminate the problem.
2026-03-11 16:45 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Collected heap and CPU profiles; preliminary suspicion: synchronous validation step in json-postprocess holds up event loop and triggers longer GC cycles.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Eng (runtime): Added instrumentation to measure per-element serialization time. Observed non-linear cost when arrays above ~800 elements; probable pathological path in JSON schema validation library.

2026-03-12 12:05 - Support (Jamie): Notified customer we are investigating and provided temporary workaround: set output_as_json:false and have client-side JSON parsing of streamed lines, or limit produced list size. Customer accepted workaround.

2026-03-13 09:00 - Eng (runtime): Patch proposed to avoid full-schema revalidation at finalization and stream-validate incrementally. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987. Running canary in staging.
2026-03-13 11:22 - SRE (Ravi): Canary in staging (eu-west) shows 10x reduction in finalization tail latency on the test cases. Scheduling prod rollout during low-traffic window.
2026-03-13 15:10 - Jamie Ortega (Support): Communicated ETA to customer for targeted prod rollout and documented recommended client-side mitigations.
2026-03-13 17:44 - Customer (BrightLedger): Confirmed workaround reduced user-visible errors; asking for permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Heap/CPU profiles point to json-postprocess worker doing bulk validation using ajv-like validator in a single pass at the end of the stream.
Proxy gateway (nginx) timeout default of 30s triggered on worst-case finalization, client saw 504 despite streaming chunks arriving earlier.
Reproducible with both redwood-instruct-3b and openchat-4x-lite; severity higher on models that emit many small tokens per element.
Hypothesis: full-document schema validation at the end creates an O(n^2) behavior due to repeated canonicalization; switching to incremental validation should be O(n).
temporary_workarounds: Customer can disable output_as_json and stream newline-delimited JSON manually from tokens.
Instruct model to emit fewer items per call or paginate results to keep arrays <800 elements.
Increase gateway timeout for customer-specific route as a short-term mitigation (requires security review).
proposed_fix: Implement incremental/streaming JSON schema validation during streaming and avoid full canonicalization at finalization. Backfill with a fast-path for large arrays that skips expensive checks when schema is simple.
next_steps: Merge runtime PR #987 and rollout canary to prod during maintenance window (assigned to Eng/runtime)
Monitor tail latency and 504 rate for BrightLedger routes for 72 hours post-rollout
Add a dashboard alert for json-postprocess finalization time >2s and automatic rollback signal
notes: Ticket created to capture customer impact and track the runtime fix. Keep customer updates weekly until resolved.
